Then write one sentence on why the same compiled file runs on Windows and Linux.

1.title: Build the solution structure
1.desc:
Write the exact sequence of commands to create a solution called Ledger containing three projects: a class library Ledger.Core, a web API Ledger.Api, and an xUnit test project Ledger.Tests.

Both Api and Tests must be able to use types from Core. Finish with a command that builds everything.
1.starter:
# Create the solution and projects


# Add them to the solution


# Wire up the project references


# Build it all
1.solution:
# Create the solution and projects
dotnet new sln -n Ledger
dotnet new classlib -o Ledger.Core
dotnet new webapi   -o Ledger.Api
dotnet new xunit    -o Ledger.Tests

# Add them to the solution
dotnet sln add Ledger.Core Ledger.Api Ledger.Tests

# Wire up the project references
dotnet add Ledger.Api/Ledger.Api.csproj reference Ledger.Core/Ledger.Core.csproj
dotnet add Ledger.Tests/Ledger.Tests.csproj reference Ledger.Core/Ledger.Core.csproj

# Build it all
dotnet build

2.title: Write a Try method
2.desc:
Write TryGetInitials following the idiomatic Try pattern: it takes a full name and produces the initials.

It returns true with the initials when the input has at least one word, and false with an empty string when the input is null, empty or whitespace. It must never throw.
2.expected:
"Ada Lovelace"   -> true,  "AL"
"Grace"          -> true,  "G"
"  "             -> false, ""
null             -> false, ""

3.title: Rules table as a switch expression
3.desc:
Rewrite this nested-if method as a single switch expression using property and relational patterns.

The rules, in priority order: amount at or below zero is "reject"; a frozen source is "reject"; same source and target account is "reject"; an amount above 1,000,000 is "refer"; anything else is "approve".
3.expected:
Amount = 0                      -> reject
Amount = 500,  frozen source    -> reject
Amount = 500,  Source.Id == Target.Id -> reject
Amount = 2,000,000              -> refer
Amount = 500                    -> approve

4.title: Make the type impossible to misuse
4.desc:
This class lets callers create nonsense: an account with no number, a negative balance, and a balance anyone can overwrite directly.

Rewrite it so that every instance is valid by construction. Requirements: the number must be supplied and non-blank; the balance cannot start negative; the balance can only change through Deposit and Withdraw; and withdrawing more than the balance throws InvalidOperationException.
4.expected:
new Account("", 100)      -> ArgumentException
new Account("ACC1", -5)   -> ArgumentOutOfRangeException
acct.Balance = 999        -> compile error
acct.Withdraw(too much)   -> InvalidOperationException
